To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CdS thin films can be etched by ammonia solution and the photocurrent of these films can be enhanced by this process.
the photoelectrochemical properties of the sprayed CdS films were improved with the etched films and that the etching process was optimized when the wetting time was about 6 h.
the surface properties of CdS films are improved by the treatment with NH3 solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behaviour of sprayed CdS films of 0.6 mu m and 2.0 mu m thickness etching in ammonia solution.
the optimisation of the surface properties of a CdS film in order to improve its photoelectrochemical behaviour.
the improvement of the photoelectrode behaviour by the use of a simple surface treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the improvement in the photoelectrochemical property is due to the levelling of the CdS film surface.
the improvement of the photoelectrochemical properties of the sprayed CdS films is obtained with a film surface treatment that leads to the formation of a thin surface layer.
this treatment leads to the destruction and the dissolution of the CdS film.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the film surface treatment applied with the ammonia solution is optimised when it takes 6-6 h and then the film surface area is increased and the photocurrent is improved.
the surface treatment applied to the CdS films leads to the improvement of the photocurrent property and that the dissolution process of the material is not a simple phenomenon.
the CdS photoelectrocatalysis is not a function of the film thickness, as far as the film thickness is less than the diffusion length of minority carriers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CdS film surface treated in an ammonia solution is a good photoanode for water splitting.
the film surface treatment is a way to control the CdS film properties.
the surface treatment of the CdS photoelectrocde is not only an efficient way to increase the electrochemical surface but also an efficient way to decrease the CdS dissolution rate.
